title: Better typography
summary: Screen type: modes, key numbers, and rules from critical to polish.

overview.purpose: Good typography reinforces the meaning of the text and conserves the reader’s attention.
overview.when: An agent is designing or building screen UI, or you are reviewing type before handoff.
takeaways: Numbers are benchmarks: deviate for a reason
Enforce while building, audit while reviewing
Contrast 4.5:1, and the layout holds at 200%

sections.title: Enforce and audit
sections.intro: Enforce while building, and audit while reviewing. If rules conflict, content and semantics win, then accessibility, language, and licensing, then intent and medium, then these benchmarks, then taste.

items.title: Enforce
items.text: When building, apply every Critical and High rule without asking.
items.more: Do it in HTML, CSS, and visible UI copy. Do not explain the typography unless asked. Paste real UTF-8. In JSX, paste the character or use {'’'}. A \u2019 escape inside tag text may render literally.

items.title: Audit
items.text: When reviewing, classify medium, language, and text role first.
items.more: Never change quotes, dashes, or spaces inside code, commands, URLs, emails, IDs, or data. Declared CSS is not proof of the rendered font or measure. Report impact, element, problem, correction, and evidence. Run Critical, then High, then Medium, then Polish. End with the three fixes that would help most.

items.title: Precedence
items.text: Content and semantics outrank the benchmarks.
items.more: Order: (1) content correctness and semantics; (2) accessibility, language, and licensing; (3) user intent and medium; (4) typographic benchmarks; (5) project taste.

items.title: Body first
items.text: Set body typeface, size, line height, and measure before headings.
items.more: Every other role is calibrated against body. Do not apply body ranges to display type. Encode roles as a reusable type scale or tokens, not one-off styles.

sections.title: Key numbers
sections.intro: Use these as starting points for screen UI, and deviate for a reason. When sources disagree, the default is listed first.

items.title: 16px body
items.text: Start UI body at 16px (1em).
items.more: Web body can sit in 15–25px, and print in 10–12pt. On screen, keep desktop at 16–24px and mobile at 16–19px. Never go below 16px on mobile, and never make mobile body smaller than desktop.

items.title: Line height 1.2–1.45
items.text: Use a unitless body line-height of 1.2–1.45.
items.more: Layouts must still hold at 1.5×. A looser web range is 1.45–1.6. Avoid a fixed pixel line-height, and avoid leading above about 1.8.

items.title: Measure 45–75
items.text: Aim for 45–75 characters per line, about 66.
items.more: A wider allowance is 45–90. Do not exceed 80. If a line goes past 75, increase line-height. 65ch is only a start, because ch measures the zero glyph.

items.title: Contrast 4.5:1
items.text: Regular text needs 4.5:1. Large text needs 3:1.
items.more: Large means 18pt (about 24px), or 14pt bold (about 18.7px). AAA for regular text is 7:1. Count secondary, placeholder, and disabled text too.

items.title: Holds at 200%
items.text: The layout must hold at 200% text size.
items.more: These are override tests, not default styles: line-height 1.5, paragraph spacing 2× the size, letter-spacing 0.12em, word-spacing 0.16em.

items.title: Caps +0.05–0.12em
items.text: Letter-space all-caps and small caps by 0.05–0.12em.
items.more: 0.06em is a common value. Smaller caps may go up to 0.2em, with extra word-spacing so words do not merge.

items.title: Two or three weights
items.text: Body sits at 400 or 500. Bold is 700.
items.more: Do not use thin or ultra-light for body text.

items.title: Two families
items.text: One capable family is often enough. Two is the maximum.
items.more: Add a third only for a distinct role, such as a monospace face for code.

sections.title: Critical
sections.intro: Run these before High, Medium, and Polish.

items.title: Body size
items.text: Start UI body at 16px, and do not go below 16px on mobile.
items.more: Keep web body in 15–25px and print in 10–12pt. Do not make mobile body smaller than desktop. Adjust for x-height, and avoid ordinary UI body above about 24px.

items.title: Line height
items.text: Body line-height is unitless, from 1.2 to 1.45.
items.more: The layout must still hold when the user sets line-height to 1.5×. Longer measures need more leading, and display type is tighter. A slightly looser web default is 1.45–1.6. Avoid a fixed pixel line-height, which headings inherit badly, and avoid leading above about 1.8.

items.title: Measure
items.text: Target 45–75 characters on a rendered English line.
items.more: About 66 is a common ideal. Stay inside 45–90, and do not exceed 80. Past 75, increase line-height. Put max-width on the text. 65ch is only an estimate. Count real lines at narrow, typical, and wide viewports, and never let prose run edge to edge.

items.title: Contrast
items.text: Regular text is at least 4.5:1. Large text is at least 3:1.
items.more: Large is 18pt (about 24px) or 14pt bold (about 18.7px). AAA is 7:1 for regular text. Apply this to secondary, placeholder, and disabled text too.

items.title: Resize and spacing
items.text: Layouts must hold at 200% text enlargement.
items.more: No clipping, overlap, or lost content, and do not disable zoom to hide overflow. Line-height 1.5, paragraph spacing of 2× the size, letter-spacing 0.12em, and word-spacing 0.16em are override tests, not the default styles.

items.title: Real styles
items.text: Load real regular, italic, and bold files.
items.more: Use WOFF2. Never rely on faux bold, faux italic, or scaled caps. Map every cut to one font-family, with its own font-weight and font-style.

items.title: Fallbacks
items.text: Every stack needs metric-aware system fallbacks.
items.more: Check the font that actually loaded, the required scripts and accents, and the layout shift when the fallback shows. size-adjust and ascent or descent overrides help.

items.title: Quotes
items.text: Use curly quotes and apostrophes in prose.
items.more: Apostrophes point down, as in don’t and ’70s. Leave straight marks in code and data, and for feet and inches unless you use true primes. Never typographically transform code, commands, URLs, or identifiers.

items.title: Dashes
items.text: Hyphen for compounds, en dash for ranges, em dash for a break.
items.more: Write 1–10 with an en dash. An em dash in prose is typically closed, or use a consistently spaced en dash. Never type --. If the sentence says “from,” write “to,” not an en dash.

sections.title: High
sections.intro: Apply these after the critical rules.

items.title: Weights
items.text: Use two or three weights, from the real font files.
items.more: Body at 400 or 500, not thin or ultra-light. Bold is 700, from the bold file.

items.title: Type scale
items.text: Build a fixed set of sizes from the body size, and reuse it.
items.more: A modular ratio such as 1.25, 1.333, or 1.5 is a guide, not a rule. Adjacent roles need a jump of at least 20–25%, or they should share one size. One worked example is body 16px and an H1 at 3em (48px). Prefer the smallest distinction that still reads.

items.title: Hierarchy
items.text: Use as few heading levels as the structure needs.
items.more: Prefer no deeper than h1–h3 in most UI. Space above a heading should exceed space below, and keep the heading with the following text. Do not underline or hyphenate headings. Prefer bold over italic. Change one or two axes at a time, size then weight.

items.title: Caps tracking
items.text: Track all-caps and real small caps at 0.05–0.12em.
items.more: 0.06em is a common value. Smaller caps may take up to 0.2em, with extra word-spacing. Keep a cap run under one line. Do not letter-space lowercase body as a general effect.

items.title: Paragraphs
items.text: Use a first-line indent or paragraph space, never both.
items.more: Do not indent the first paragraph after a heading. Indent about 1–1.5em, or up to 1–4× the size. Paragraph space is about 50–100% of the font size. 0.75em is a common web space.

items.title: Alignment
items.text: Left-align running web prose.
items.more: Center only a short title or quote, under one line. Justify only with language-aware hyphenation and a wide enough measure. Never letter-space a line to justify it.

items.title: Emphasis
items.text: Use one signal at a time: bold or italic, not both.
items.more: Keep the emphasis shorter than a sentence when you can. Do not underline text that is not a link. Do not use quotes or all caps for emphasis, and do not emphasize a whole paragraph.

items.title: Ellipsis and spaces
items.text: Use the ellipsis character, and one space between sentences.
items.more: Write …, not three periods. Never use two spaces after a sentence. Use a non-breaking space in © 2026, § 12, Fig. 3, honorifics, and short numeric labels.

items.title: Numerals
items.text: Use tabular lining figures, right-aligned, for tables and aligned quantities.
items.more: Proportional or oldstyle figures may be used in running prose when the font has them.
items.css: td.num { font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums lining-nums; text-align: right; }

items.title: Responsive type
items.text: Measure and leading do not change with the screen size.
items.more: Scale font-size and the container width together. clamp(16px, 2.5vw, 20px) is a starting pattern. Give text at least 1rem of side padding on small screens. Scale display headings down. Do not shrink body, subheads, or controls.

items.title: Caption floor
items.text: 12px is a floor for non-essential captions only.
items.more: Do not add tracking to save small type. Never use 12px for text the user must act on.

sections.title: Medium
sections.intro: Apply these after Critical and High.

items.title: Families
items.text: One capable family is often enough. Two is the practical maximum.
items.more: A third face is only for a distinct role, such as code. Give each family one job. Do not set body text in a novelty, script, or monospaced face.

items.title: OpenType
items.text: Keep kerning on, and use standard ligatures in prose.
items.more: Leave discretionary ligatures off in body text. Turn ligatures and character substitutions off in code. Use real small caps, with about 0.05em of tracking. Never fake small caps. Confirm the loaded font actually includes the feature.

items.title: Symbols
items.text: Use ©, ™, and ® only when you mean them.
items.more: © takes a non-breaking space and the year. Do not write “Copyright ©”. Use × for multiplication and a true minus when the math is clear. Prefer primes for measurements when the system has them. Otherwise keep straight foot and inch marks, never curly quotes. A missing accent is a font failure.

items.title: Lists, quotes, tables
items.text: Use semantic lists, and let hanging lines wrap with the text.
items.more: Set a block quote apart with an indent of about 2–5em or with space, not stacked decoration, and drop the extra quotation marks. Prefer cell padding and a thin header rule over heavy table borders. Pad cells about 0.5em 1em.

items.title: Loading
items.text: Prefer WOFF2, and a variable font where it helps.
items.more: Choose a loading policy that avoids invisible text and a jump in layout. font-display: swap is a solid default. If the font has an optical-size axis, check it at the rendered size. Use text cuts for body and display cuts for large type.

items.title: Links and color
items.text: A link must be identifiable without color alone.
items.more: Do not style ordinary text so it looks like a link. Avoid pure black on pure white. In dark mode, use off-white on dark, not pure white on black, and retune the weight: slightly heavier, or slightly lighter. Both are sourced.

items.title: Language
items.text: Set lang and direction on the document and on mixed-language runs.
items.more: This drives hyphenation, quotation marks, and fallback fonts.

items.title: UI casing
items.text: Prefer sentence case for headings, buttons, labels, and navigation.
items.more: Apply it consistently across the product.

sections.title: Polish
sections.intro: Apply these after Critical, High, and Medium.

items.title: Display type
items.text: At 48px and up, tighten line-height and tracking.
items.more: Lines should not gape, and descenders must not collide with the next line.

items.title: Widows
items.text: Keep the last two words of a headline together.
items.more: Use a non-breaking space on headlines and short UI strings. text-wrap: balance is for headings. pretty is for body, not for short strings. For print, set orphans and widows to 2. Full widow control of web body is not always practical.
items.css:
h1 { text-wrap: balance; }
p { text-wrap: pretty; }

items.title: Hanging punctuation
items.text: Hang opening quotes on block quotes and display lines where you can.
items.more: A hair space or a thin space around an em dash helps when a full space is too wide.

items.title: Link underline
items.text: If you underline links, keep the stroke thin.
items.more: Use a 1px thickness and a 2px offset.

sections.title: RTL and Hebrew
sections.intro: Set the language and the direction, and do not copy English spacing onto Hebrew.

items.title: From the sources
items.text: Set lang and dir for each run of text.
items.more: Do not apply English rules for letter-spacing, hyphenation, justification, quotation marks, or emphasis to an unfamiliar script. Mixed Hebrew or Arabic with Latin or numbers needs a bidirectional check, not a guess from source order. Extra tracking can break a joining script. Arabic is called out for that.

items.title: Practice, not a sourced rule
items.text: Do not letter-space Hebrew, and do not italicize it.
items.more: Give Hebrew body a slightly taller line-height than the Latin range. These three points are practice. They are not stated as rules in the sources. Confirm them with a Hebrew reference and with rendered samples before you treat them as hard rules.

sections.title: Before you finish
sections.intro: Check these before handing off a UI or a typography review.
items: Body size, unitless line-height, and rendered measure checked at narrow, typical, and wide viewports
Contrast meets 4.5:1 and 3:1, and the layout holds at 200% zoom and at 1.5 line-height
Real weights and italics load, fallbacks are metric-aware, and there are no faux styles
The type scale and two or three weights are consistent, with at most two families plus mono for code
Prose uses curly quotes, correct dashes, ellipses, and non-breaking spaces, and code and data are untouched
Caps are tracked, lowercase body is not, and tables use tabular lining figures
Paragraphs use indent or space, not both, and headings have more space above than below
Prose is not edge to edge, text does not hit the screen edge, and links are not color-only
Kerning is on, standard ligatures are on in prose and off in code, and small caps are real
The layout still works under the spacing overrides, not only at the default styles
lang and dir are set, and required scripts have the glyphs
